ground_truth: The redemption process creates uncollateralized YUSD. It sends the full collateral back to the user first, then takes a fee in YUSD. This fee-YUSD is left without backing, which will lead to a gradual de-peg and insolvency of the stablecoin[cite: 2719, 2730].

If a redemption request is canceled after collateral has been moved to the minting contract, the funds become stuck with no way to return them. These stuck funds can then be mistaken for protocol profit, leading to the minting of uncollateralized YUSD [cite: 2807, 2834, 2837-2839].

A malicious whale can grief the protocol by consuming the entire periodic redemption limit with requests and then canceling them. Because the limit is not credited back upon cancellation, this creates a Denial of Service, blocking all legitimate users from redeeming their YUSD for the duration of the period[cite: 2862, 2865, 2887].
